summary: Iteration 5 backend testing: 3 new features validated via /app/backend/tests/test_features_v4.py (35 tests). 25 PASS, 10 FAIL. All 10 failures are a single critical implementation gap: the contador_readonly_guard middleware described in the review request is NOT registered in server.py. Contador users can perform mutations on non-admin-guarded endpoints (200 OK on POST /api/customers, /api/leads, etc.). Fiscal regime DB persistence (including survival across `supervisorctl restart backend`) verified. Product goals CRUD + upsert + progress math (achieved_qty=3, achieved_amount=300.00, progress_pct derived correctly) verified. Contador login, read access on 8 read endpoints, CSV scoping (contador==admin), and register-contador role all pass.

critical.issue: contador_readonly_guard middleware is NOT registered in /app/backend/server.py. Only CORSMiddleware is added. Contador role can therefore perform mutations on any endpoint that isn't explicitly protected by require_admin: POST /api/customers -> 200 (record created), POST /api/leads -> 200 (record created), POST /api/orders reaches business logic (400 only because payload invalid, not because auth blocked). Endpoints guarded by require_admin correctly return 403 but with detail='Admin access required' instead of the spec's 'Contador é somente-leitura'. No global allowlist covering only /api/auth/login, /api/auth/logout, /api/notifications/* is enforced.

minor.issue: Endpoint not implemented — returns 405 Method Not Allowed. If deletion is intended (as implied by contador write-block spec), it needs to be added; otherwise remove from spec.
Numeric(6,4) storage rounds rates like 0.00825 to 0.0083 causing small reverse-math discrepancies. Not user-facing.

action_items: IMPLEMENT contador_readonly_guard middleware in /app/backend/server.py. Suggested implementation: @app.middleware('http') that inspects request.method (block POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) and current user's role. Allowlist paths: /api/auth/login, /api/auth/logout, /api/notifications (prefix). Extract JWT from Authorization header, decode with JWT_SECRET, look up user role; if role == 'contador' AND method in mutation set AND path not in allowlist -> return JSONResponse(status_code=403, content={'detail': 'Contador é somente-leitura'}).

Once middleware is added, re-run tests/test_features_v4.py::TestContadorWriteBlocked — all 10 parametrized cases should turn green (except the DELETE /orders/nonexistent case which needs the DELETE order endpoint to exist, or drop that test).
Optional: standardise 403 detail message across auth failures (currently mixes 'Admin access required' vs 'Contador é somente-leitura' expectation).
critical_code_review_comments: settings_store.py + fiscal.current_mode() cleanly resolves the previous iter-4 race concern: mode is now read from an in-memory cache backed by the settings table; persistence survives supervisor restart (verified end-to-end).

goals_router.product_goal_progress correctly aggregates from order_items joined to orders (seller_id + status in invoiced/confirmed + created_at within month). Vendedor scoping applied via WHERE user_id = current.id. Upsert on (user_id, product_id, month) also works.
auth_router.register accepts role='contador' — 'contador' is in the allowed set alongside admin/vendedor.
reports_router correctly treats admin and contador as identical scoping (see all invoices) while vendedor is scoped to own — verified by row-count parity between admin and contador CSV.
MISSING: server.py has no contador middleware. This is the single blocker preventing the 'read-only role' feature from meeting its security spec.
auth_router.py:34 sets role via `role = payload.role if payload.role in (...)` — good defensive filter.

rca of the issue: server.py imports the required modules (settings_store, auth) but never registers a mutation-guard middleware for the contador role. The `auth.is_contador` helper is defined but only used by reports_router for scoping — no global mutation block. All contador-mutation-blocked tests fail because the request reaches the handler and either succeeds (endpoints only requiring get_current_user) or is rejected by require_admin with the wrong message. Fix: add an @app.middleware('http') block in server.py that decodes the JWT, checks role=='contador' with method in {POST,PATCH,PUT,DELETE} and path not in allowlist, and returns 403 with detail='Contador é somente-leitura'.
